sentences.text:
Order 
This bail application is filed under section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.486 of 2025 of Chandera Police Station, Kasargod,
registered for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 376AB and 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860, apart from Sections 3(a), 4(2), 5(l), 5(p) 5(m) and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. According to the prosecution, petitioner, who is the victim's father's brother-in-law had, during the period from 2019 to 2022, committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim aged 14 years and thereby committed the offences alleged.
Petitioner was arrested on 12.06.2025, and he has been in custody since then.

4. Heard Sri. Ramesh Chander, the learned Senior Counsel, instructed by Sri. Bejoy Joseph P. J. the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri. Prasanth M. P., the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.

The learned Senior Counsel submitted that investigation has already been completed and the final report has also been filed, and therefore, considering the period of custody already undergone by the 2025:KER:74174 petitioner from 12.06.2025, further custody ought not be permitted.

The learned Senior Counsel also pointed out that the victim had in fact filed another complaint as Crime No.487 of 2025 before the same Police Station, raising allegations of a similar nature against another relative, and the Sessions Court had granted bail to the said accused as early as on 15.09.2025.

It was also submitted that since the victim had raised similar allegations against two persons in relation to offences allegedly committed during the period 2019 to 2022, the belated filing of the complaint itself indicates a false allegation having been raised.
It was also pointed out that there are property disputes between the family members, and the complaint is the result of such disputes as well.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, opposed the application and submitted that petitioner's earlier bail application filed as B.A. No.10460 of 2025 was dismissed on 28.08.2025,
and no change of circumstances has been pointed out.
It was also submitted that considering the close relationship between the petitioner and the victim, there is every chance that the petitioner would influence the witnesses if he is released on bail.

sentences.text: When the matter came up for consideration on 29.09.2025, this Court directed the Investigating Officer to serve notice on the victim, considering that the offences under Section 376AB of IPC is incorporated.
Though notice has been served on the victim through her father on 04.10.2025, there is no representation on her behalf.
8. On a consideration of the rival contentions , it is noticed that 2025:KER:74174 the incident is alleged to have taken place during the period from 2019 to 2022.
The complaint was filed only in June 2025, and the petitioner was arrested on 12.06.2025.

Though this Court had, on an earlier occasion, dismissed the bail application of the petitioner after noticing that there is an old hymenal tear, indicating penetrative sexual assault, the learned Senior counsel handed over a copy of the order in Crl.M.C. No.1407 of 2025 of the Special Court for Atrocities Against Women and Children,
Kasargod, wherein the accused in Crime No.487 of 2025 of Chandera Police Station was granted bail.

entities.text:
Special Court for Atrocities Against Women and Children,
Kasargod
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A perusal of the said order indicates that the very same victim had made similar allegations against another close relative for having committed penetrative sexual assault on her during the same period.

The accused in the said crime was arrested on 11.06.2025 and he was released on bail on 15.09.2025.
9.
The pendency of such a crime was not brought to the notice of this Court on the earlier occasion.

The grant of bail to the accused in Crime No.487 of 2025 of Chandera Police Station and the nature of allegations against both the accused being almost similar, I am of the view that the grant of bail to the said accused can be treated as a change of circumstances warranting consideration of this bail application.

10. Since petitioner has been in custody from 12.06.2025, and reckoning the alleged property dispute between the families of the petitioner and the victim, apart from the grant of bail to the accused in Crime No.487 of 2025 of Chandera Police Station, I am of the view that 2025:KER:74174 petitioner can also be released on bail on strict conditions.
11.

Accordingly, this bail application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(a) Petitioner shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.

(c) Petitioner shall not enter into the jurisdictional limits of Chandera Police Station,
till the conclusion of trial.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence or contact the victim or her family members.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
